newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan stocks close lower after main share peak.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan stocks close lower after main share peak.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed lower on Monday in flat trade as some of the leading stocks lost ground and others remained stable, traders said.
The all-share index closed 0.22 percent lower, at 437.03 points compared with 437.99 points on Friday.
"Most leading stocks which had peaked in the last weeks became too expensive for potential buyers that's why they are decreasing now, this is a natural phenomenon," said one Casablanca-based trader.
Wafabank, one of the liquid stocks, and Spanish-Moroccan Uniban bank closed unchanged, respectively at 546 and 110 dirhams.
SNI, Morocco's second largest private conglomerate, shed five dirhams at 555 dirhams.
Morocco largest private ONA Group fell five dirhams to trade at 495 dirhams, traders said. The group ceded its 86.25 percent in maize derivatives producer SOMADIM to British-Belgian group Amylum.
Traded volume on the official market was 19.9 million from 25.9 million dirhams on Friday.
